CAUSE, precisely: the split's resolver contract landed as a TEST-ONLY file. tests/Shared/KeepverseRoots.cs resolves gk-data/gk-core roots and is Compile Include'd into every *.Tests project by Directory.Build.props, but production src/ has zero references to GkDataRoot, GkContentRoot, KeepverseRoots or WorkspaceRoots, and 6 of the 7 FindUp call sites are in src/. MSBuild knows the workspace roots; the running program does not. This is the 393-item content-root-consumer residue class made visible as a test failure, and it is the one blocking proof row that a build alone would have reported green. FIX LOCATION: the source repository, then re-stage and re-apply. residue.json marks every one of these items allowedFix=source, so editing the split output would fork the corpus from its source. Condition 10 measured: NOT MET, and the four generators cannot run at all in the split layout. All four exit 2 (could-not-start), not 1 (stale), so this is a resolution failure and not drift. CreatureSpeciesGen and CreatureBuildPlanGen: 'could not locate data/tuning; needed to load the shipped balance surface'. FamilyExpandGen: 'missing gk-data/packs/fusion/data/seed/affix-families'. TreeBinder: 'Could not find a part of the path D:\Works\source\Keepverse\data\tuning\power-scale.v2.json' - it walked up from the working directory to the workspace root and looked for data/tuning there, which is where it lived in the monorepo. Where the pieces actually landed: data/tuning is gk-core/data/tuning (202 files); seed affix-families is gk-data/packs/fusion/data/seed/items/affix-families (16 files). SAME ROOT CAUSE as condition 8's test failure, and that is the finding: the split gave MSBuild knowledge of the workspace roots and no runtime knowledge. THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THE FIX TRACTABLE: gk-forge/tools/seedsmith/seedsmith/workspace_roots.py already exists and already encodes the intended design - content_root(), core_root(), a _layout() that detects monorepo versus Keepverse, an env override, and the rule 'Nothing found raises; a root is never guessed'. It even names its twin: 'A copy of this module lives at gk-core/scripts/lib/keepverse_roots.py; keep the two identical.' There is NO C# equivalent: searching gk-core/src and gk-forge for a root or workspace resolver returns nothing, and src/ has zero references to GkDataRoot, GkContentRoot, KeepverseRoots or WorkspaceRoots. The only C# resolver is the test-only tests/Shared/KeepverseRoots.cs, Compile Include'd into every *.Tests project. So Python tooling can find the workspace and the compiled program cannot. Note the MSBuild layer DOES work - the gk-core build copies data/seed/** into bin/Debug/net8.0 - so the breakage is confined to code that resolves a root at runtime or from the current directory. CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: conditions 8 (tests) and 10 (generators) are one fix, not two, and both are downstream of the rules change Lane 3 owns, because a re-stage before that would run twice.

ADDITION 5's violation is not confined to gk-tests, and it is roughly thirty times the scale. ownership.v1.json carries 'scripts/**' -> gk-core at priority 0, whole repo. Two workflow scripts were carved out to root at priority 10 (scripts/session-boundary-check.py, scripts/audit-doc-citations.py) and the catch-all swept the rest. By ADDITION 5 every one of those is gk-workflow's single source of truth. scripts/verification-boundaries.v1.json is the sharpest instance: the plan itself called it 'wrong the moment there are nine repos', and it sits in gk-core. It hid from a rule-name scan, which reported ZERO violations, because the pattern is scripts/** and matches nothing by name. A pattern-name scan is how this hides. NOT FIXED, on purpose: moving ~130 files needs a re-stage and a re-apply across seven repositories, and the content-root finding needs the same cycle. Staging twice would double the one operation in this migration that is not a dry run and whose delete loop already cost 209 files. Both change sets land first, then one stage and one apply. Checked and deliberately NOT changed: .github/workflows/ci.yml and nightly.yml -> gk-core at priority 10 is consistent with ADDITION 5, since a CI file a platform requires inside a sub-repository is exactly the thin entrypoint the principle permits.

The content-root-consumer residue class has a production fix now, in the SOURCE repo, commit 285a7a957. Root cause, one sentence: the split gave MSBuild the workspace roots and the running program none. Directory.Build.props grew GkDataRoot/GkContentRoot so the build is green, while SeedImportRunner.FindUp still walked up from the current directory - and after the split that walk stops at the gk-core checkout while data/seed lives in a sibling gk-data pack. It reached data/tuning by luck because gk-core owns that, which is why nothing looked broken until content was read. The contract already existed and was correct (tools/seedsmith/seedsmith/workspace_roots.py, which even names its twin and says 'a root is never guessed'); what was missing is that tests/Shared/KeepverseRoots.cs was the ONLY C# implementation and it is linked into *.Tests alone. A resolver only the tests can see is a resolver the product cannot use. ADDED src/FusionRpg.Core/Workspace/KeepverseRoots.cs (net6.0, Unity-free, no SQL; guard-dal and guard-secondary-no-unity both OK), mirroring the Python contract exactly. One deliberate difference, documented in the type: Roots() returns BOTH candidate roots, because FindUp is handed data/seed and data/tuning by different callers, cannot tell which owns a path, and they live in different repositories after the split - so the filesystem decides and no convention is hardcoded. SeedImportRunner.FindUp gains a pre-pass and KEEPS its walk, because a monorepo checkout must return byte-identical answers and dist/FusionRpg.Server/data (a real call site in AtomImporter and CreatureSpeciesImport) is in neither root. TESTS 15 green: 9 in FusionRpg.Core.Workspace.Tests, 6 in FusionRpg.Data.Tests, both layouts and both resolvers asserted to agree. The seed subset of FusionRpg.Data.Tests is 117/117. The first draft of these tests went into FusionRpg.Core.Tests, which was wrong twice over - FusionRpg.Core.Workspace.Tests already existed and already held a KeepverseRootsTests, so it would have been a duplicate class and namespace in a second assembly. Deleted, not shipped. TWO BLOCKS, both reported rather than worked around. (1) The boundary mapping for the new files is DEFERRED: src/FusionRpg.Data/Seed/SeedImportRunner.cs is owned by NO boundary row and reaches verification only through the data-fallback and seam fallbacks, which is the unmapped-production-path defect; the mapping was written and then REVERTED because scripts/verification-boundaries.v1.json is claimed by the active session ps1-ban-manager-20260926 (direct mode, features/mega-merge, 1107 paths). The registry is byte-identical to HEAD, sha256 b9d0a8ed4e0d80bd72c0bd3a768d807788d6c2e8cfdc6787206744812b9529b1, and nothing of theirs was touched. (2) verify-change.py aborts before running ANY test on this repo: it runs the session-boundary guard unscoped and three other active sessions contribute drift that fails it, while the same guard scoped to this session exits 0 and states the drift 'does not block it'. The plan's checks were therefore run directly - dal OK, test-substrate OK, session-boundary OK (scoped), Guard.Tests 717 passed / 4 failed, all four proven independent of this change (the registry is byte-identical to HEAD and none of the four tests references any file this session touched). STILL NOT MET: conditions 8 and 10. The fix is in the source repo; gk-core holds the pre-fix tree. They close only when this is re-staged and re-applied, and that re-stage must share a cycle with the scripts/** carve-out.

A LANE'S COMMITS LAND AFTER ITS REPORTED DEATH, AND ONE OF MY COMMIT MESSAGES IS THEREFORE WRONG. Lane 3 (gk-tests topology) was reported as errored twice with a transport Headers Timeout. It had in fact committed twice before the error surfaced, and both commits are in gk-workflow's history on main, which I have been pushing: b4d359e 'docs: the plan and the rules now name the same topology for gk-tests' (created docs/gk-tests-topology-reconciliation.md at 276 lines and also touched the plan and the lane-setup notes) and 888fd44 'docs: record the provenance gap honestly instead of guessing at it' (rewrote section 4 of the lane-setup notes again). Neither is mine. CONSEQUENCE: my commit dbba30c, 'docs: reconcile the gk-tests topology, and record the larger finding it exposed', carries Lane 3's version of the document, not the one I wrote. The file blob at dbba30c and at HEAD is identical (686224b9d300), so the content I described in that message - a seven-section document with a four-row refusal table and a scripts section - is not what that commit contains. Its own description of correcting section 4 was also overtaken: 888fd44 rewrote that section again after me. WHY IT MATTERS: this is the third time in this migration that a provenance claim was asserted without the command that settles it, and the first time it was in MY OWN commit message rather than in a report. The earlier two were a count that excluded copies and an A7 scan whose needles matched code paths. The pattern is the claim; the surface varies. I also wrote a PowerShell ancestry test that reported b4d359e and dbba30c as unrelated because 'if (git merge-base --is-ancestor ...)' tests the command's OUTPUT, which is empty, not its exit code - so it printed 'no' for a pair that is in fact linearly ordered. A broken test that returns a confident wrong answer is worse than no test. NOT AMENDED, per the no-amend rule. Corrected here and in the follow-up commit instead. LANE 3's own work stands on its merits and was reviewed, not discarded: its seal design is sound, its 14 tests all fail against the pre-change tool, its section 8 independently measured the same 132-file scripts figure I measured, and it had already recorded the finding with an owner and a reason. The commit added on top of it adds the evidence that changes the reason from 'deferred pending a judgement about 132 files' to 'the obvious move breaks gk-core's build and its standalone clone', with the four-part change set that has to happen instead - including that two of the six consumers are .ps1 files the ps1-ban program is already retiring and must not be given a new home. LANE RESTART RULE, restated because it is now measured rather than assumed: a lane that dies on a transport error may have already committed. Before restarting a lane, read git log for its fence and check whether its work is already at HEAD. Restarting blind risks a second lane redoing or contradicting the first.

The fix closed ZERO residue ids, and that is the honest reading. content-root-consumer went 393 -> 394: the +1 is my own new TEST file (tests/FusionRpg.Data.Tests/Seed/SeedImportRunnerFindUpTests.cs), flagged for naming data/seed and data/tuning as the segments it asserts on. The production resolver src/FusionRpg.Core/Workspace/KeepverseRoots.cs was NOT flagged - the file that fixes the problem is clean and the file that proves it is counted, because the detector matches literal paths and cannot tell 'resolves a content path wrongly' from 'names a content path correctly'. Same family as the ip-censor fixture. THE STRUCTURAL POINT, which needs an owner ruling and is not mine to take: the detector greps for literals, so a fix that works by making the existing literals RESOLVE CORRECTLY cannot lower the count. Rewriting 393 call sites by hand to use GkDataRoot is the prescribed allowedFix=source remedy, and it would be the worse outcome - more churn, more places to diverge, when one resolver pre-pass already makes every one of them correct in both layouts. So the queue is arguably mis-specified rather than merely open: it should be closable 'resolved by construction' with the resolver named, and the detector should learn that a call site of the resolver is not itself a violation. Recorded as an open item with its owner, NOT closed and NOT exempted. No guard was weakened to move a number.

CONDITION 8 REMAINS NOT MET, and the blocker is now measured at full scale. gk-core builds clean with every private sibling absent (75 projects, 0 errors, 34s) - that half holds. The test half does not, and the cause is NOT the resolver just shipped. Measured: 175 files under gk-core contain a hand-rolled FindRepoRoot() that throws DirectoryNotFoundException("repo root"), and 140 of them identify the repo root by the existence of src/FusionRpg.Injector - a directory the split moved to gk-fusion. 14 more look for CONTRIBUTING.md, which in the split resolves to the WORKSPACE root rather than gk-core, and 9 look for src/FusionRpg.Core, which is correct. So the majority marker is a cross-repository reference created by the split. THE COMPOUNDING DEFECT, which matters more than the marker: roughly 37 of those files carry a [ModuleInitializer]. A module initializer that throws runs at ASSEMBLY LOAD, so one unresolvable path fails EVERY test in the assembly - observed directly: FusionRpg.Core.Workspace.Tests failed 9 of 9 with System.TypeInitializationException from '<Module>' before a single test body ran, and FusionRpg.E2E.Tests failed 296 of 296 the same way. That converts 'this environment lacks gk-data' into 'the whole suite is red', which is why the original 296/296 looked like a product bug and was not one. A module initializer must never throw; resolution belongs in the test that needs it.
